sourceNote: Names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation list as published via Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guides, kinds, missable flags and roadmap stages are this guide's own work, derived from those official descriptions.

trophies.guide: The platinum unlocks automatically once the other 54 trophies are yours, so there is nothing to do for this one directly. Work through the roadmap in order — story first, then stranger strands, collectibles, activities and crime — and save the 100% completion trophy for last, because it is the longest grind standing between you and this one. Nothing about it can be missed: every other trophy is either story progress or free-roam work you can return to.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, from the start of the game until its closing cutscene — it is the first mission, so this is the first trophy most players earn. Follow the on-screen prompts and do not skip the mission; there is no way to fail into missing it, but it only counts when the mission itself completes. Missable in the story sense: it belongs to this one mission, so finish it on your first pass rather than rushing past it.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1. Chapters complete in order, so just keep playing the main story — side activities and free-roam detours do not block it, but the trophy only pops when the chapter's final mission ends. Treat it as a milestone, not a task: if you are doing side content, come back to the story to push the chapter over the line.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2, in the same way as Chapter 1. The chapter trophy pops at the end of its final mission, so the only requirement is story progress. Use the chapter break as a natural moment to bank side progress — collectibles, vehicle discoveries and challenge counts all carry over, so a detour here costs nothing.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3. By now the map is wide open, which makes it tempting to drift into free roam for hours — that is fine, but remember this trophy only moves when the story does. If you want the platinum efficiently, keep a steady rhythm: a chapter, then a batch of side content, then the next chapter.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 4, the last chapter before the finale. This is the last chapter trophy, so once it pops you are one mission away from the story's gold trophy. Before the final mission, it is worth clearing any story-adjacent side strands you care about, since the finale is the natural point where many players switch to free-roam cleanup.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Play the final story mission to its end — this is the gold trophy for finishing the story, and it pops when the mission's closing scene plays. It is the last story trophy, so before you start it, grab anything that can only happen during the story: the named-mission trophies earlier in this list are all behind you by now, but stranger-strand finales and collectibles can wait for free roam. After it pops, the whole map is yours for cleanup.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. It is a single named mission, so the trophy is tied to that one playthrough: finish the mission and the trophy pops at its end. If a mission goes wrong mid-way, restart it from the pause menu rather than abandoning the story thread — the trophy only counts a completed run of this mission.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions tend to have setup steps before the main event, so expect a longer mission — the trophy still only cares that you finish it. Stock up on armour and ammo before you start, and play it in one sitting if you can; a failed attempt costs nothing but time, since you can retry the mission.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Like every named-mission trophy, it pops when that mission ends, so the method is simply to play the mission through. It sits in the story sequence, so you will reach it naturally — the only way to miss it is to stop playing the story, and the fix is to pick the story back up.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. The name suggests a big set-piece, so go in prepared and follow the mission's objectives rather than improvising — straying from the script is the usual way a mission run falls apart. Finish it once, cleanly, and the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around Vice City International Airport. Airport missions usually mean tight spaces and heavy resistance, so keep a good weapon ready and use cover. The trophy pops at the mission's end, and like the other named missions it is a one-mission job: finish VCIA Takedown and you are done with it.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation name points to a military-style set-piece, so expect a longer, combat-heavy mission and bring your best gear. It is the last of the named-mission bronzes, so once it pops, every story trophy left is a chapter trophy or the finale itself.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the in-game completion checklist — story missions, stranger strands, collectibles, activities and the counted challenges, all of it. This is the long one: treat it as the sum of every other trophy rather than a separate task, and use the pause menu's stats screen to find which category is still short. It cannot be missed, only left unfinished, so chip away at the thinnest categories first and save this gold for the run-up to the platinum.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, drifts, near misses, air time and other driving feats — anywhere in Leonida, in any vehicle. The count is cumulative across the whole playthrough, so every jump you land while travelling counts; do not grind it in one sitting early on, because story driving alone will bank a large share. For the final stretch, pick a fast car and a stretch of road with ramps and jumps, and chain stunt after stunt. The pause menu's stats screen shows your running count.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample all 9 activity types at least once: racing, fishing, arcade games, shooting range, drone races, bowling, meditation, darts or pool-style bar games, and the other open-world pastimes the game offers. You do not need to win or master any of them — one try each is enough. Work through them early, because each one you try also starts progress toward its own dedicated trophy, and the activity markers on the map show you where each type lives.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Score gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Each challenge is a timed accuracy drill, so the method is practice, not luck: learn the target pattern, keep your aim steady, and restart a challenge the moment a run goes bad rather than finishing a silver run. Use a weapon you are comfortable with and take the challenges one at a time — gold in all 42 is a skill trophy, and the last few will be the hardest. This is the silver that most players will grind last among the activities.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 race locations across Leonida. Each location is its own race, so work through them on the map one by one and tick them off. Drone races reward clean lines over speed alone: learn each course's corners, cut them tight, and avoid crashing, because a crash costs more time than a cautious corner ever will. The race markers show which locations you have already won.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — road, off-road, boat and air races all count, as long as each one is a race you have not won before. The word different matters: replaying the same race does not add to the count. Spread your wins across race types and locations, and use the map's race markers to find ones you have not tried. A fast, well-handling car and a clean first lap are usually enough against the field.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Take on Cal in a fishing challenge and beat him. Fishing challenges are about reading the line and reeling steadily rather than mashing the controls — keep tension in the safe zone and tire the fish out before you haul it in. If you lose, challenge him again: this is a skill contest you can retry as often as you like, so treat each attempt as practice for the next one.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Find an arcade — they are marked on the map in Vice City and other towns — and finish one arcade game from start to end. Any game counts, so pick the shortest or the one you enjoy most. You do not need a high score, just a completed run, which makes this one of the quickest bronzes in the list and a good first activity trophy.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Play through Andy's mission strand until his final mission, then complete it. Stranger strands unlock as you meet characters around Leonida, and each one ends with a finale mission that carries its own trophy. The trophy is tied to that finale: finish Andy's last mission and it pops. If you have not met Andy yet, keep exploring — stranger markers appear as you travel, and his strand will open in time.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Play through Kenton's mission strand until his final mission, then complete it. Like the other character finales, this trophy belongs to one mission — Kenton's last — so the method is to follow his strand to its end. Strands can be easy to overlook while the main story pulls you forward, so check your map for stranger markers between story missions and clear them as you go.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Play through Billy's mission strand until his final mission, then complete it. Billy's strand is one of five character finales in the list, and each one is a self-contained story with its own trophy. Do his missions when they appear rather than letting them pile up — a strand finished early is one less thing to chase in the endgame.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Finish 8 full mission strands for strangers — the odd characters you meet across Leonida, marked on the map. Each strand is a short chain of missions ending in a finale, and this silver counts finished strands, not missions. Work through stranger markers whenever they appear, because strands unlock gradually and the five named finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) count toward the 8. Keep a mental note of which strangers you have finished so the last ones are easy to find.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Play through Randy's mission strand until his final mission, then complete it. Randy's finale is one of the five named stranger finales, and like the rest it is a single mission with a trophy attached. His strand involves supply runs, so expect driving and delivery work along the way — steady driving beats fast driving when the cargo matters.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Play through Tyrone's mission strand until his final mission, then complete it. Tyrone's finale is the last of the five named stranger finales; once it pops, the stranger section of your checklist is nearly done. If his marker has not appeared yet, keep playing the story — strands open up as the map and story progress, and his will come.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Find all 18 meditation spots across Leonida and meditate at each one. Meditation spots are quiet scenic places, often on hilltops, beaches and viewpoints — the map and your travels will reveal them, and each one you use counts. This is a calm collectible: no combat, no timer, just visiting all 18. Pair it with the exploration trophy, since the same road trip that opens up the map will carry you past most of the spots.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Take on Bret's hunt and bring down the unique animal he asks for. Hunting in Leonida means tracking: follow the trail, watch the animal's behaviour, and take a clean shot rather than a rushed one — a wounded animal that escapes costs you the trail. The hunt is a side strand, so it sits outside the main story; start it when Bret's marker appears and finish it in the same trip if you can.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Finish 3 complete sets of collectible cards, found as hidden pickups across Leonida. Cards are tucked into corners, rooftops, alleyways and interiors, so the hunt is about exploring thoroughly rather than rushing — check behind buildings and up stairways as you pass through each area. A set only counts when every card in it is found, so keep a checklist of which sets are one or two cards short and sweep those areas again. This silver pairs naturally with the exploration trophy.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK feature at 100 different locations — it is the game's photo or social-sharing spot check-in, done at marked viewpoints and landmarks. The count needs 100 distinct locations, so do not repeat the same spot: each new place you visit is a chance to tick one off. Work it into your exploration runs and your collectible hunts, because the same road trip covers WAiNK spots, card pickups and meditation spots at once.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Finish 50 challenges of any kind — the game's open-world challenge list spans driving, shooting, flying, exploration and more. Challenges complete passively as you play, so this bronze is a slow burn: play widely, try everything, and the count climbs on its own. If it stalls near the end, open the challenges menu and pick off the easiest unfinished ones — short, specific tasks like a single stunt or a quick race are the fastest way to close the gap.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Build a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then lose the cops and escape. The partner matters: your companion has to be in the car or beside you when the heat rises and when it breaks. Earn the stars with a crime spree, then break line of sight, switch vehicles, and lay low until the wanted level fades — alleys, tunnels and the countryside all help. If the level drops before you escape, build it back up and try again.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner alongside, rob three shops in a row without ever losing your wanted level in between — the chain breaks if the heat drops to zero, so keep the pressure on. Plan a route through three nearby shops, hit them fast, and keep moving: lingering in one place lets the cops close in, while a quick getaway keeps the chain alive. A fast car parked outside each shop is the difference between a chain of three and a chain of one.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — drive them, and they count as discovered. Leonida's roads are full of variety, so this one grows naturally as you travel, but you can speed it up by trying every new car, bike, boat and truck you see rather than sticking to one favourite. Parked cars in different districts, traffic on the highways and vehicles at events are all new discoveries. Check the stats screen to see how close you are.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Activate Combat Focus — the slow-motion aiming mode — and take down 5 enemies before it ends. The trick is to set the scene first: gather a group of enemies, then trigger Focus with a full weapon and pick your targets fast. A busy shootout or a gang hideout gives you the crowd you need; a quiet street will not. If you only manage three or four, reload the moment and try again with a bigger group.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Leave Vice City International Airport in an unscheduled way — that is, take a plane out without going through the normal departures. Steal an aircraft from the tarmac or the hangars and get airborne before security shuts you down. It is a stunt as much as an escape: grab the plane, throttle up, and do not stop for anything. A small, fast aircraft is easier to steal and lift off than a big jet.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Deal with the Rhinos — the military tanks that roll in when the heat is at its worst. This trophy is about surviving a tank encounter: get a wanted level high enough to bring the Rhinos out, then handle them, whether that means destroying one, stealing one, or simply living through the encounter. Bring heavy weapons and keep moving, because a tank's cannon does not miss twice. It is a chaos trophy, so expect a loud, expensive afternoon.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store cleanly, without any detection. Stealth is the whole job: case the store first, move quietly, avoid cameras and staff sightlines, and get out before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails — leave, lose the heat, and come back for a clean run. Plan your entry and your exit before you walk in, and do not bring a loud weapon to a quiet job.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Vault robberies are bigger jobs than shop robberies: expect alarms, armed response and a getaway under pressure, so plan the escape route before you crack the vault. Each vault counts only if you get away clean, so a fast car and a route that breaks line of sight matter as much as the robbery itself. Work through the vaults one at a time across your free-roam sessions.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Stop an armored truck, rob it, and escape. Armored trucks patrol the roads, so watch for them in traffic and pick a quiet stretch to make your move — block the truck, force it open, grab the cash, and leave before the response arrives. A sticky bomb or a heavy weapon stops the truck fast; a fast getaway car finishes the job. One clean robbery is all it takes.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Visit all 52 areas of Leonida, from Vice City's streets to the swamps, beaches and small towns of the state. Areas count when you enter them, so this trophy is earned by travelling: drive the highways, take the back roads, and detour into every settlement you pass. The map shows which regions you have covered, so the last few areas are a matter of checking the map for blank patches and driving out to them. Pair it with the vehicle and WAiNK counts on the same road trips.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs in Leonida. Each gang runs its own operations — stash houses, deals and fronts — marked around the map, and you need one from every gang, not nine from the same one. Learn which gang holds which territory, hit one operation per gang, and get out clean each time. This is the trophy that teaches you the map's gang geography, so it pairs well with the exploration trophy.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Head to Ocean Beach, find a bar or vendor with a view of the water, and enjoy a cocktail there. This is a flavour trophy — no combat, no timer, just being in the right place and doing the right small thing. Ocean Beach is the long strip of sand and hotels on Vice City's east side, so walk the beachfront until you find a spot serving drinks with a view, sit down, and order one.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive into a vehicle showroom and smash your way back out through the glass, in classic GTA style. Pick a showroom, pick a fast car, and do not stop once you are through the doors — the trophy is about the spectacle of the exit, so commit to it. Expect a wanted level and a repair bill, and expect to laugh: this one is a deliberate callback to the series' oldest chaos, and it pops the moment you burst out onto the street.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and bowl a proper game — follow through on your throw, as the description puts it. Bowling is one of the game's activities, so the method is simply to play it: pick up a ball, aim, and roll. You do not need a strike or a high score, just a completed visit to the lanes. It is a quick, relaxed bronze and a good palate cleanser between the harder grinds.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: Reach a partnership moment with mass appeal — a story or relationship beat where the duo's partnership lands in front of a crowd. This is a story-adjacent trophy tied to a specific moment in the game, so it will come as you play through the main thread and the partner missions. Keep playing the story and the partner content, and it pops when the moment arrives; there is no grind attached to it, only progress.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Make choices — 500 of them, as PlayStation's counter tracks. Choices happen all through the game: dialogue options, approach decisions in missions, how you handle strangers and side content. The count climbs with normal play, so do not chase it directly early on; just play, choose, and let it accumulate. Near the end, if it is still short, replay missions with different choices and take every dialogue option you previously skipped.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Succeed on a second try — fail something, then get it right the next time. This trophy is almost a joke at the player's expense: everyone fails something eventually, so the method is to fail once at a mission, challenge or activity, then complete it on the immediate retry. If it has not popped by the time you are deep into the game, pick any activity you have failed before and beat it on the second attempt.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Witness something strange — Leonida is full of odd encounters, easter eggs and random events, and this trophy is for stumbling into one of them. There is no single marked location: explore the weird corners of the map, visit remote spots at odd hours, and follow anything that looks out of place. The strange event will find you if you keep exploring, and the trophy pops the moment you see it.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by — attack from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon. Get a vehicle alongside a target on foot, lean out, and swing: the trophy needs the knockdown to come from the melee hit while you are driving. A slow car on a quiet street gives you the time to line it up; a fast car on a highway does not. One clean hit is enough, so set it up carefully rather than swinging wildly.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists, and your contacts turn that dirty money clean for a cut — keep feeding them bills until the laundered total reaches $250,000. This is a long-economy trophy, so it grows alongside the crime trophies: rob vaults, trucks and operations, collect the Marked Bills, and launder them regularly rather than letting them pile up. The contacts menu shows your running total.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — clothes, weapons, food, vehicles, anything sold in a store. The total is cumulative across every shop in the game, so it climbs as you gear up normally: buy the weapons you need, the outfits you like, and the snacks that keep you going. If it is still short in the endgame, a shopping spree on expensive items closes the gap fast, and the money comes back through the crime and laundering trophies.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties across Leonida. Garages are property purchases, marked on the map, and each one gives you somewhere to store vehicles — so they are worth buying for the storage alone. They cost money, so this trophy waits until your economy is healthy: laundered heist money and robbery income will cover it. Buy them as you can afford them, and the trophy pops when the eighth deed is yours.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the in-game delivery and rideshare app. Open the app, register a vehicle you own or have found, and repeat until 10 are listed. Any vehicles count, so use the cars you already drive daily plus a few you pick up along the way. It is a quick endgame mop-up: if you have been discovering vehicles for the other trophy, ten registrations is a few minutes of menu work.
trophies.name: On the Spot
